import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 513

*Reference:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/513](https://www.erdosproblems.com/513)
 - [ClHa64] Clunie, J. and Hayman, W. K., The maximum term of a power series. J. Analyse Math.
  (1964), 143-186.
-/

open scoped Nat Real
open Filter Polynomial

namespace Erdos513

noncomputable def ratio (r : ℝ) (f : ℂ → ℂ) : ℝ :=
  (⨆ n, ‖iteratedDeriv n f 0 * (n ! : ℝ)⁻¹ * r ^ n‖) / (⨆ z : {z : ℂ // ‖z‖ = r}, ‖f z‖)

/-- Let `f` be a transcendental entire function. What is the greatest possible value of
`liminf (fun r : ℝ => ratio r f) atTop`? -/
@[category research open, AMS 30]
theorem erdos_513 : answer(sorry) =
    ⨆ f : {f : ℂ → ℂ // Transcendental ℂ[X] f ∧ Differentiable ℂ f},
    (liminf (fun r : ℝ => ratio r f) atTop) := by
  sorry

/-- For all transcendental entire function `f`, `liminf (fun r : ℝ => ratio r f) atTop ≤ 2 / π - c`
for some `c > 0`. This is proved in [ClHa64]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem erdos_513.variants.upper_bound : ∃ c > 0,
    ⨆ f : {f : ℂ → ℂ // Transcendental ℂ[X] f ∧ Differentiable ℂ f},
    (liminf (fun r : ℝ => ratio r f) atTop) ≤ 2 / π - c := by
  sorry

/-- For all transcendental entire function `f`, `liminf (fun r : ℝ => ratio r f) atTop > 1 / 2`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem erdos_513.variants.lower_bound :
    ⨆ f : {f : ℂ → ℂ // Transcendental ℂ[X] f ∧ Differentiable ℂ f},
    (liminf (fun r : ℝ => ratio r f) atTop) > 1 / 2 := by
  sorry

end Erdos513

findings.description: The docstring at line 52 says that every transcendental entire function has liminf(ratio) > 1/2. The Lean theorem correctly says that the supremum of these liminfs is > 1/2, equivalently that some such function has liminf > 1/2. The universal assertion in the docstring is false: for f(z) = exp(z), the ratio at positive integer radii m is m^m/(m! e^m), which tends to 0 by Stirling's formula, so its liminf is 0.
findings.source_evidence: He–Tang, arXiv:2602.12217v1, §1, defines B = sup_f liminf μ(r,f)/M(r,f) and states: “Kövári (unpublished) observed that in fact B > 1/2.” Hayman–Lingham, arXiv:1809.07200v2, Problem 2.14(c), likewise asks for the exact upper bound β and records 4/7 < β < 2/π. These are lower bounds on the extremal constant, not on every function.
findings.suggested_fix: Change only the docstring to say that the supremum is greater than 1/2, or that there exists a transcendental entire function f with liminf(ratio r f) > 1/2. Keep the Lean statement unchanged.

reformulations.difference: The admissible class, also used in both variants, is expressed as Transcendental ℂ[X] f ∧ Differentiable ℂ f rather than as an entire function that is not a polynomial.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The actual polynomial-algebra instance sends p to the function z ↦ p.eval z. Thus algebraicity means a nonzero polynomial relation P(z,f(z)) = 0. Every polynomial function satisfies such a relation. Conversely, an entire algebraic function has polynomial growth: outside a sufficiently large disk, the leading coefficient of P in its second variable is nonzero, and a polynomial-root bound bounds |f(z)| by a power of |z|. Cauchy's estimates then imply that f is a polynomial. Consequently, within the entire functions, this transcendence predicate is exactly non-polynomiality. Differentiable ℂ f expresses complex differentiability everywhere, hence entire holomorphy.

reformulations.difference: The source uses Taylor coefficients and maxima, whereas Lean uses iterated derivatives divided by factorials and real indexed suprema. The helper also accepts nonpositive radii.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For an entire function, a_n = f^(n)(0)/n!. For r > 0 the numerator's terms therefore equal |a_n| r^n. These terms tend to zero, so their supremum is the maximum term. Continuity on the nonempty compact circle makes the denominator's supremum its maximum modulus. Cauchy's estimate gives 0 ≤ ratio ≤ 1 for positive radii, so the real liminf and the outer real supremum are well-defined without unbounded-set defaults. Values at nonpositive radii do not affect the limit at +∞. Lean tests proved the coefficient normalization, these bounds, and the negative- and zero-radius behavior; the complete source-to-helper equivalence was not formalized.

reformulations.difference: The literature records B < 2/π; Lean writes ∃ c > 0, B ≤ 2/π − c, where B is the supremum of the liminfs.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A positive c with B ≤ 2/π − c implies B < 2/π. Conversely, if B < 2/π, take c = 2/π − B. This equivalence was proved in Lean for arbitrary real B. The supremum form also gives a uniform bound on every admissible function, since the family is nonempty and bounded.

review.notes: All four declarations were checked. The formal mathematical statements are faithful; the sole finding is a docstring quantifier error. The current source still marks the main problem OPEN. Both bound variants remain known results; subsequent improvements to the lower bound do not invalidate their solved tags. The inaccessible Clunie–Hayman full text was corroborated using Hayman's problem collection and He–Tang's introduction. /workspace/review/scratch.lean and /workspace/review/bounds.lean compile and test polynomial exclusion, coefficient normalization, boundary cases, supremum equivalences, and boundedness. In particular, the ratio and liminf bounds were proved without sorryAx. The reviewed file remains byte-for-byte identical to the committed file.
